questions.question: A child on a stationary skateboard throws a ball forwards at high velocity, and the child and skateboard move backwards at a lower velocity. Explain, in terms of momentum, why they move backwards more slowly.
questions.answer: The backward momentum of the child and skateboard equals the forward momentum of the ball, but their mass is much larger, so their velocity is smaller.
steps: Before the throw the total momentum is zero (both stationary).
Conservation of momentum: the forward momentum of the ball equals the backward momentum of the child and skateboard.
The two momenta are equal in magnitude, so the momentum of each is the same.
Momentum = mass x velocity, so velocity = momentum / mass.
The child and skateboard have a much larger mass than the ball, so their velocity is much lower.

questions.question: Trolleys X (mass m) and Y (mass 3m) travel towards each other at the same speed v, collide and move off together. Which statement is correct? A: force of X on Y greater than Y on X; B: force of X on Y less than Y on X; C: speed of X after collision greater than v; D: speed of X after collision less than v.
questions.answer: D: the speed of X after the collision is less than v
steps: Newton third law: the forces X and Y exert on each other are equal and opposite, so A and B are wrong.
Take Y's direction as positive: momentum before = 3mv - mv = 2mv.
Trolleys move off together with combined mass 4m, so their common speed = 2mv / 4m = v/2.
Speed of X after the collision = v/2, which is less than v, so D is correct.

questions.question: Trolley A (mass m) runs down a frictionless slope from height h, then a frictional force F stops it over distance d on the horizontal track. Derive an expression for the gradient of the graph of d against h, in terms of F, m and g.
questions.answer: Gradient = mg / F
steps: Gravitational potential energy lost on the slope = mgh.
On the horizontal track the work done against friction = Fd.
Energy conservation (no energy lost before the horizontal track): mgh = Fd.
So d = (mg/F) h, which is a straight line through the origin with gradient mg/F.

questions.question: Identical trolley B is at rest at the bottom of the slope. Trolley A rolls down, collides with B, and they move off together at velocity v. Assess whether the student's prediction (stated in the PDF) was correct, ignoring friction.

questions.question: A 0.17 kg mallet travelling at 1.6 m/s hits a stationary 0.035 kg disc. After the collision the mallet moves on at 0.3 m/s in the same direction, and the disc moves at v in that direction. Calculate v, ignoring friction.
questions.answer: v = 6.3 m/s (in the same direction as the mallet)
steps: Momentum before = 0.17 x 1.6 = 0.272 kg m/s (the disc is stationary).
Momentum of mallet after = 0.17 x 0.3 = 0.051 kg m/s.
Conservation of momentum: 0.272 = 0.051 + 0.035v.

questions.question: A 0.035 kg disc at 5.0 m/s at the bottom of a 30 deg ramp travels 6.5 cm up the ramp before stopping and sliding back. Determine the frictional force acting on the disc.
questions.answer: About 6.6 N
steps: Kinetic energy at the bottom: (1/2)mv^2 = 0.5 x 0.035 x 5.0^2 = 0.438 J.
At the highest point the disc is at rest, so its kinetic energy is zero.
Gain in gravitational potential energy: mgd sin30 = 0.035 x 9.81 x 0.065 x 0.5 = 0.0112 J.
Work done against friction = 0.438 - 0.0112 = 0.426 J (energy transfer, as the friction does work over distance d).
Friction F = work / distance = 0.426 / 0.065 = 6.6 N.

questions.question: Spheres P and Q are identical. P moves on a smooth surface and hits stationary Q. After the collision P has momentum 0.096 kg m/s at 15 deg to its initial direction and Q has momentum 0.14 kg m/s at 10 deg (on the other side). Show that the total momentum after the collision is about 0.2 kg m/s.
questions.answer: Total momentum after the collision = 0.23 kg m/s (about 0.2 kg m/s), along the initial direction of P.
steps: Take P's initial direction as the x-axis; the two spheres move off on opposite sides of it.
y-components: 0.096 sin15 - 0.14 sin10 = 0.0248 - 0.0243 = 0.0005 kg m/s, which is effectively zero.
Resultant = sqrt(0.2306^2 + 0.0005^2) = 0.23 kg m/s, which is about 0.2 kg m/s, as a scaled vector diagram would show.

questions.question: State the principle of conservation of linear momentum.
questions.answer: For a closed system with no resultant external force, the total (vector) momentum before an interaction equals the total momentum after it.
steps: The principle applies to a system on which there is no resultant external force.
The total linear momentum of the system before an interaction equals the total momentum after it.
Momentum is a vector, so this is true for components in each direction.

questions.question: Sphere P has mass 0.12 kg and Q is initially stationary. Calculate the initial velocity of sphere P.
questions.answer: About 1.9 m/s
steps: Q is stationary, so the total momentum before the collision is that of P alone.
By conservation of momentum this equals the total momentum after: 0.2306 kg m/s.
Initial velocity of P = momentum / mass = 0.2306 / 0.12 = 1.9 m/s.

questions.question: Water is 14% of the total mass of a kernel of mass 0.11 g. The steam is ejected downwards and the popped kernel moves upwards at 1.5 m/s. Calculate the speed of the ejected steam.
questions.answer: About 9.2 m/s (downwards)
steps: Mass of steam = 0.14 x 0.11 g = 1.54 x 10^-5 kg.
Mass of popped kernel = 0.86 x 0.11 g = 9.46 x 10^-5 kg.
Total momentum is zero before popping, so the momentum of the kernel upwards equals the momentum of the steam downwards.

questions.question: Which quantity has SI base units kg m^2 s^-3? A: force; B: momentum; C: power; D: work done.
questions.answer: C: power
steps: Power = work done / time, and work done = force x distance, which has units kg m^2 s^-2.
Power = (kg m^2 s^-2) / s = kg m^2 s^-3.
Force is kg m s^-2, momentum is kg m s^-1, and work done is kg m^2 s^-2, so only power matches.

questions.question: Object A (2 kg) moves right at 3 m/s and object B (5 kg) moves left at 2 m/s before they collide. What is the total momentum of A and B after the collision? A: 4 kg m/s left; B: 4 kg m/s right; C: 16 kg m/s left; D: 16 kg m/s right.
questions.answer: A: 4 kg m/s to the left
steps: Take right as positive. Momentum of A = 2 x 3 = +6 kg m/s.
Momentum of B = 5 x (-2) = -10 kg m/s.
Total momentum (conserved) = 6 - 10 = -4 kg m/s, i.e. 4 kg m/s to the left.

questions.question: Bumper car P (250 kg) moves at 2.10 m/s and hits stationary car Q. Afterwards P moves at 1.15 m/s and Q at 1.57 m/s, both in the same direction. Show that the mass of Q is about 150 kg.
questions.answer: Mass of Q = 151 kg, about 150 kg
steps: Momentum before = 250 x 2.10 = 525 kg m/s (Q is stationary).
Momentum after = 250 x 1.15 + M x 1.57 = 287.5 + 1.57M.
Conservation of momentum: 525 = 287.5 + 1.57M, so 1.57M = 237.5.

questions.question: State one assumption made in the calculation in part (a)(i).
questions.answer: No external forces act on the cars (friction and air resistance are negligible), so momentum is conserved.
steps: Conservation of momentum applies only when there is no resultant external force.
So the assumption is that friction and air resistance on the cars are negligible during the collision.

questions.question: The collision lasts 1.35 s. Calculate the average horizontal force on Q during the collision.
questions.answer: About 176 N (about 180 N to 2 s.f.)
steps: Change in momentum of Q = final momentum of Q - 0 = M x 1.57 = 237.5 kg m/s.
This equals the momentum lost by P: 250 x (2.10 - 1.15) = 237.5 kg m/s.
Newton second law: average force = change in momentum / time = 237.5 / 1.35 = 176 N.

questions.question: Explain why car P decelerates during the collision, referring to Newton's laws of motion.
questions.answer: Q pushes P backwards with a force equal and opposite to the force P exerts on Q (third law); this net backward force on P gives it a backward acceleration (second law).
steps: During the collision P exerts a forward force on Q (Newton third law pair).
Q exerts an equal and opposite force backwards on P.
This backward force is a resultant force on P opposite to its motion.
By Newton second law the resultant force gives P an acceleration opposite to its velocity, so it slows down.

questions.question: State the principle of conservation of momentum (in the context of speed skaters colliding).
questions.answer: In a closed system with no resultant external force, the total momentum before a collision equals the total momentum after it.
steps: The system is the skaters, with no resultant external force acting on them during the collision.
The total momentum before the collision equals the total momentum after it.
Momentum is a vector, so this applies to each direction separately.

questions.question: Skater A (65 kg, 5.5 m/s) is hit from behind by skater B (60 kg, 7.5 m/s). B locks his arms around A and they move on together at 6.2 m/s. Deduce whether momentum is conserved.
questions.answer: No: momentum before is 807.5 kg m/s but after is 775 kg m/s, so momentum is not conserved for these values.
steps: Momentum before = 65 x 5.5 + 60 x 7.5 = 357.5 + 450 = 807.5 kg m/s (both skaters moving in the same direction).
Momentum after = (65 + 60) x 6.2 = 125 x 6.2 = 775 kg m/s.
The totals differ by about 33 kg m/s (about 4 %), so momentum is not conserved for the values given.

questions.question: Explain the decrease in kinetic energy in this inelastic collision between the skaters.
questions.answer: Some kinetic energy is transferred to other forms, such as internal (thermal) energy and sound, during the collision, e.g. in the locking and deformation of the skaters.
steps: In an inelastic collision the skaters stick together, so the collision is not perfectly elastic.
Kinetic energy is not conserved, so energy is transferred to other stores.
Energy is transferred to internal (thermal) energy and sound by the deformation and friction during the collision.
The total energy is conserved; only the kinetic energy decreases.

questions.question: State the principle of conservation of momentum for an aluminium sphere colliding head-on with a stationary steel sphere.
questions.answer: In a closed system with no resultant external force, the total momentum before the collision equals the total momentum after it.
steps: The two spheres form a closed system with no resultant external force.
Total momentum before the collision equals total momentum after it.

questions.question: The aluminium sphere (2.7 kg) moves at 10.0 m/s and hits a stationary steel sphere (7.9 kg). Immediately after the collision the steel sphere moves at 5.0 m/s in the original direction. Calculate the velocity v of the aluminium sphere after the collision.
questions.answer: v = -4.6 m/s, i.e. 4.6 m/s in the opposite direction to its original motion (it rebounds)
steps: Take the initial direction of the aluminium sphere as positive.
Momentum before = 2.7 x 10.0 = 27 kg m/s.
Momentum after = 2.7v + 7.9 x 5.0 = 2.7v + 39.5 kg m/s.

questions.question: A carriage of mass 7.15 x 10^4 kg moving at 4.50 m/s collides with and joins a carriage of mass 5.35 x 10^4 kg. They move at 3.62 m/s afterwards. Show the total momentum after the collision is about 4.5 x 10^5 kg m/s.
steps: Total momentum after = 1.25 x 10^5 x 3.62 = 4.525 x 10^5 kg m/s.
This is about 4.5 x 10^5 kg m/s, as stated.

questions.question: Calculate the velocity of the second carriage (mass 5.35 x 10^4 kg) before the collision, using the total momentum after the collision.
questions.answer: About 2.4 m/s in the same direction
steps: Momentum before = 7.15 x 10^4 x 4.50 + 5.35 x 10^4 x v = 4.525 x 10^5 kg m/s (conservation).
v = 1.3075 x 10^5 / 5.35 x 10^4 = 2.44 m/s, in the same direction.

questions.question: Calculate the change in total kinetic energy during the collision between the two railway carriages.
questions.answer: Change = -6.5 x 10^4 J (kinetic energy decreases by about 65 kJ)
steps: The kinetic energy decreases by about 65 kJ, as energy goes into deformation and heat in the coupling.

questions.question: State the principle of conservation of linear momentum, in the context of an asteroid absorbing another asteroid.
questions.answer: For a closed system with no resultant external force, the total linear momentum before an interaction equals the total momentum after it.
steps: The two asteroids form a closed system with no resultant external force.
Total linear momentum before the collision equals total linear momentum after it.

questions.question: Asteroid A has velocity 2.19 x 10^3 m/s and momentum 1.80 x 10^17 kg m/s. Show that its mass is about 8.2 x 10^13 kg.
steps: Momentum = mass x velocity, so mass = momentum / velocity.
This is about 8.2 x 10^13 kg, as stated.

questions.question: Asteroid B (mass 5.90 x 10^12 kg, velocity 15.0 x 10^3 m/s) is absorbed by asteroid A (mass about 8.2 x 10^13 kg, velocity 2.19 x 10^3 m/s). Calculate the velocity of the asteroids after the collision.
questions.answer: About 3.05 x 10^3 m/s (about 3.1 km/s) in the direction of the original motion
steps: Momentum of A = 1.80 x 10^17 kg m/s; momentum of B = 5.90 x 10^12 x 15.0 x 10^3 = 8.85 x 10^16 kg m/s.
Total momentum before = 1.80 x 10^17 + 0.885 x 10^17 = 2.685 x 10^17 kg m/s.

questions.question: Which of the following is an SI unit for momentum? A: kg m s^-1; B: J m^-1; C: m s^-2; D: N s^-1.
questions.answer: A: kg m s^-1
steps: Momentum = mass x velocity, so its unit is kg m s^-1.
J m^-1 is the unit of force (energy per distance), m s^-2 is acceleration, and N s^-1 is the unit of rate of change of force.
So A is the correct unit.

questions.question: A tennis ball launcher on frictionless wheels is stationary before a ball is fired horizontally. Explain, in terms of momentum, why the machine starts to move.
questions.answer: Total momentum is zero before firing, so the ball's forward momentum must be balanced by an equal backward momentum of the machine.
steps: Before firing, the total momentum of the ball and machine is zero.
The ball gains forward momentum when it is launched.
By conservation of momentum the machine must gain an equal and opposite (backward) momentum.
The machine has no friction to stop it, so it moves backwards and starts to move.

questions.question: A tennis ball of mass 0.056 kg is launched at 4.5 m/s from a machine of mass 2.9 kg. Calculate the velocity of the machine just after the ball is launched.
questions.answer: About 0.087 m/s, in the opposite direction to the ball
steps: Total momentum before launch = 0 (both at rest).
Momentum of ball = 0.056 x 4.5 = 0.252 kg m/s forwards.
Momentum of machine must be 0.252 kg m/s backwards (conservation).
Velocity of machine = 0.252 / 2.9 = 0.087 m/s, backwards.

questions.question: Explain, referring to Newton's laws, why the velocity of the descent module changes when its rocket motor ejects hot gases at high velocity.
questions.answer: The motor pushes gas backwards, and by Newton third law the gas pushes the module forwards; the resultant force gives the module an acceleration (second law), changing its velocity.
steps: The rocket motor accelerates hot gases backwards (ejected at high velocity).
Newton third law: the gas exerts an equal and opposite force on the motor and descent module, pushing the module in the other direction.
This force is a resultant force on the descent module.
Newton second law: the resultant force produces an acceleration, so the velocity of the module changes.

questions.question: The descent module's velocity changes by 0.58 m/s in 5.0 s when the rocket motor operates. The descent module has mass 2950 kg. Calculate the average force exerted on the hot gas.
questions.answer: About 342 N (equal in size and opposite to the force on the module)
steps: Momentum change of descent module = 2950 x 0.58 = 1711 kg m/s.
Average force on module = 1711 / 5.0 = 342 N.
By Newton third law the average force exerted on the hot gas is equal in size and opposite in direction, so it is 342 N backwards.

questions.question: State the principle of conservation of linear momentum, as demonstrated with two gliders on an air track.
questions.answer: For a closed system with no resultant external force, the total linear momentum before an interaction equals the total momentum after it.
steps: The gliders on the air track form a closed system with no resultant external force.
The total linear momentum before the collision equals the total linear momentum after it.

questions.question: Gliders A and B have equal masses. A moves towards stationary B, they stick together, and the velocity after the collision is half the velocity of A before. Deduce whether the results show momentum is conserved.
questions.answer: Yes: momentum before = m v and after = 2m x (v/2) = m v, so momentum is conserved.
steps: Before the collision: momentum = m x v (only A moves; B is stationary).
After the collision: combined mass = 2m, and velocity = v/2.
Momentum after = 2m x v/2 = mv, which equals the momentum before.
So the results show that momentum is conserved.

questions.question: Explain why the force of attraction between the two magnets did not affect the momentum demonstration.
questions.answer: The magnetic force acts between the two gliders, which are both inside the system; the forces are equal and opposite, so they do not change the total momentum of the system.
steps: The magnetic force acts between A and B, so both forces are internal to the system of gliders.
By Newton third law, the force on A from B is equal and opposite to the force on B from A.
The two internal forces cancel in the total, so the total momentum of the system is unchanged.
Only external (resultant) forces could change the system's total momentum, and there are none.

questions.question: A graph shows how the velocity of a skittle varies with time during its collision with a ball. Determine the average acceleration of the skittle during the collision.
questions.answer: Needs the velocity-time graph from the PDF to read the initial and final velocities and the collision time.

questions.question: Explain how Newton's second and third laws apply to the ball and the skittle during the collision.
questions.answer: The ball and skittle exert equal and opposite contact forces on each other (third law); each force produces an acceleration of the object it acts on, with a = F/m (second law).
steps: During contact the ball exerts a force on the skittle, and the skittle exerts an equal and opposite force on the ball (Newton third law).
The two forces are the same type (contact) and act on different bodies, for the same time.
The force on the skittle gives it an acceleration in the direction of the ball's motion, so it moves off (Newton second law).
The force on the ball is opposite to its motion, so the ball decelerates.
Each object's acceleration is a = F/m, so the same force gives a larger acceleration to the object with the smaller mass.
The change in momentum of each object equals the impulse (force x time) it receives from the other, consistent with the second law.

questions.question: A ball's horizontal velocity changes from 7.2 m/s to 1.6 m/s when it hits a stationary 1.4 kg skittle, which then moves at 3.1 m/s in the same direction. Determine the mass of the ball.
questions.answer: About 0.78 kg
steps: Momentum before = m x 7.2 (skittle stationary).
Momentum after = m x 1.6 + 1.4 x 3.1 = 1.6m + 4.34 kg m/s.
Conservation: 7.2m = 1.6m + 4.34, so 5.6m = 4.34.

questions.question: During the collision there is a resultant force on ball B from ball A. Explain, in terms of Newton's laws, why ball A decelerates.
questions.answer: Ball B exerts an equal and opposite force on ball A (third law); this force opposes A's motion, so by second law A decelerates.
steps: Ball A exerts a force on ball B in the direction of motion (Newton third law pair).
Ball B exerts an equal and opposite force on ball A, backwards, opposing its motion.
This backward force is the resultant force on A.
By Newton second law, a resultant force opposite to the velocity produces a deceleration of ball A.
